meta.scalability_note: Single primary region (Nuremberg); VMware-based infrastructure with manual scaling; no serverless compute; no auto-scaling groups; limited horizontal elasticity for dynamic workloads
meta.performance_note: BSI IT-Grundschutz certified; ISO 27001; 99.95% uptime SLA; German Tier-3 data centers in Nuremberg; strong compliance posture for regulated industries

AWS Amplify.note: No managed web or mobile application hosting platform. Applications are deployed on VMware-based VMs or Kubernetes.

AWS Lambda.note: No FaaS or serverless function service. Event-driven compute workloads must be implemented on VMs or Kubernetes Jobs.

Amazon ECS.note: No managed container orchestration service equivalent to ECS. Container deployments are handled via Kubernetes only.

Amazon EKS.note: Kubernetes is available as a managed service but with limited managed features; the primary infrastructure is VMware vSphere-based rather than cloud-native.

Amazon EC2.note: Enterprise VM hosting on VMware vSphere with flexible vCPU and RAM configurations. Suited for enterprise and regulated workloads.

AWS Batch.note: No managed batch job processing service. Batch workloads require manual orchestration on VMs or Kubernetes Jobs.

AWS Elastic Beanstalk.note: No PaaS application deployment platform. All deployments are managed by the customer on VMs or Kubernetes.

Amazon S3.note: S3-compatible object storage service available within the noris data center environment.

Amazon S3 Glacier.note: No dedicated archive or cold storage tier. Long-term data retention relies on standard object or block storage.

Amazon EBS.note: SAN-based block storage with high IOPS for enterprise VM workloads. Persistent and attachable to virtual servers.

AWS Backup.note: VM-level backups and snapshots are available as a managed service. No unified cross-service backup policy management equivalent to AWS Backup.

Amazon EFS.note: No managed elastic NFS-compatible shared file system. Shared storage solutions must be self-hosted.

Amazon RDS.note: Managed database hosting is available as a managed service, limited to MySQL and PostgreSQL. Less automated failover and scaling compared to AWS RDS.

Amazon DocumentDB.note: No managed MongoDB-compatible document database. Self-hosting required on VMs.

Amazon DynamoDB.note: No managed NoSQL key-value or wide-column database. Self-hosted DynamoDB-compatible services must be deployed on VMs.

Amazon Timestream.note: No managed time-series database service. Self-hosted InfluxDB or TimescaleDB must be deployed.

Amazon Aurora.note: No managed high-performance Aurora-compatible relational database. Managed databases are limited to standard MySQL and PostgreSQL.

Amazon ElastiCache.note: No managed in-memory caching service. Redis or Memcached must be self-hosted on VMs.

Amazon Redshift.note: No managed cloud data warehouse. Analytical workloads require self-hosted solutions on VMs.

AWS Application Load Balancer.note: Load balancing is available but HTTP/HTTPS routing configuration is less self-service and feature-rich than AWS ALB. Managed via support request.

AWS Network Load Balancer.note: TCP load balancing is available. Advanced features and self-service configuration are limited compared to AWS NLB.

Amazon VPC.note: VLAN-based isolated private networking with firewalls, custom routing, and segmentation for enterprise workloads.

Amazon Route 53.note: DNS services are available but advanced routing policies such as latency-based or geolocation routing are limited compared to Route 53.

Amazon API Gateway.note: No managed API gateway service. API management must be self-hosted using tools such as Kong or nginx.

Amazon CloudFront.note: No CDN service available. Content delivery requires third-party CDN providers.

AWS Direct Connect.note: Dedicated MPLS lines and colocation cross-connects available for private, high-bandwidth connectivity to the noris data center.

Amazon Rekognition.note: No managed computer vision or image/video recognition service. Self-hosted or third-party AI APIs required.

Amazon SageMaker.note: No managed ML training or inference platform. ML workloads must be deployed manually on VMs.

Amazon Bedrock.note: No managed generative AI or foundation model API. Self-hosted LLM deployments on GPU infrastructure required.

AWS Glue.note: No managed ETL or data integration service. Data pipelines must be self-hosted.

Amazon EMR.note: No managed big data processing cluster. Hadoop or Spark must be self-deployed on VMs.

Amazon Athena.note: No serverless query service for object storage. Self-hosted Trino or Presto required.

AWS IAM.note: User and role management is available via the customer portal. Permission granularity is less fine-grained than AWS IAM; resource-level policies are limited.

Amazon Cognito.note: No managed identity and user pool service for applications. Self-hosted Keycloak or similar is required.

AWS IAM Identity Center.note: No managed SSO or centralised identity federation service.

AWS KMS.note: No managed key management service. Encryption key management relies on self-managed solutions or third-party HSM integration.

AWS Secrets Manager.note: No managed secrets storage or automated rotation service. HashiCorp Vault or similar must be self-hosted.

AWS Certificate Manager.note: TLS certificate management is available via the portal. Certificate renewal is a manual process; no automated lifecycle management equivalent to ACM.

Amazon GuardDuty.note: No managed intelligent threat detection service. External SIEM tools must be integrated for security monitoring.

AWS Security Hub.note: No unified security posture management or findings aggregation dashboard.

AWS Config.note: No managed resource configuration compliance and continuous audit service.

AWS Shield.note: Network-level DDoS protection is provided at the data center level. No advanced application-layer DDoS mitigation equivalent to AWS Shield Advanced.

AWS WAF.note: No managed web application firewall service. WAF capabilities require self-hosted solutions.

AWS CloudTrail.note: No managed API activity logging or audit trail service. Infrastructure-level audit logging is managed by noris internally but not exposed as a customer-facing service.

Amazon CloudWatch.note: Infrastructure metrics and alerting provided via a Zabbix-based monitoring platform. Less integrated and with fewer data sources than CloudWatch; no log aggregation service.

Amazon SNS.note: No managed pub/sub notification service. Alerting notifications are delivered via email or SNMP from the monitoring platform.

AWS Systems Manager.note: No managed operations management platform for patching, inventory, or session management. These functions are handled by noris as part of managed services.

AWS Cost Explorer.note: Detailed billing and cost reports per service are available in the customer portal with monthly and resource-level breakdowns.

AWS CodeBuild.note: No managed CI build service. CI/CD pipelines must use self-hosted or external tools such as GitLab CI or Jenkins.

AWS CodeDeploy.note: No managed application deployment automation service.

AWS CodePipeline.note: No managed CI/CD pipeline orchestration service.

Amazon ECR.note: No managed container image registry. Customers must deploy and operate their own registry such as Harbor or Docker Registry.

AWS CloudFormation.note: No native IaC templating service. Infrastructure automation relies on external tools; Terraform with VMware or noris APIs is the recommended approach.

AWS IoT Core.note: No managed IoT device gateway or connectivity service. IoT brokers must be self-hosted on VMs.

AWS IoT Device Management.note: No managed IoT device fleet management or over-the-air update service.

Amazon SQS.note: No managed message queue service. RabbitMQ or Apache Kafka must be self-hosted on VMs.

Amazon EventBridge.note: No managed event bus or event routing service.

AWS Step Functions.note: No managed serverless workflow orchestration service. Workflow automation requires self-hosted Apache Airflow or similar.

Amazon SES.note: No managed transactional email sending service. Third-party SMTP providers or self-hosted mail infrastructure required.

Amazon Kinesis.note: No managed real-time data streaming service. Self-hosted Apache Kafka or Redpanda required.
